prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Daft Punk Get Lucky" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

blindly4 commands (for reference; you use the actions above):
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

steps: Precondition: Chrome is open on a youtube.com page (any, e.g. watch?v=...). Target the Chrome window via blindly4.

Step 1 (find search box): find --title Search --role combobox --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Pick the AXComboBox with title="Search" (NOT the AXTextField titled 'Address and search bar'). Record its path as SEARCH_BOX.
Step 2 (type query): set-value --path SEARCH_BOX --value "<song query>" --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.

Step 3 (submit): press the search button, which is the sibling right after the combobox: same path as SEARCH_BOX with the last index changed from ...0.0.0 to ...0.0.1 (found via find --title Search --role button). Use --expect-description Search. Prefer re-finding it with find --title Search --role button rather than computing the path.
Step 4 (wait for results): wait 2000 ms (results render asynchronously; the first find may be empty/truncated otherwise).

Step 5 (find result): find --role link --title "<key words of song title>" --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Choose the first AXLink whose id="video-title" and whose value starts with https://www.youtube.com/watch. Its title contains the video name plus duration. Skip links to channels, playlists (list=RD...) only if a better plain watch link exists; otherwise the first match is fine.
Step 6 (play): press --path RESULT_PATH --expect-description "<video title fragment>". Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 7: wait 3000 ms for the watch page to load.
Step 8 (verify): find --title Pause --role button --depth 40 --limit 3 --format xml. Success = an AXButton titled "Pause (k)" exists (video is playing). If instead 'Play (k)' appears, press it.
Total: 2 finds before typing is avoidable: do 1 find for the combobox, set-value, press search (4 calls), then find result, press, wait, verify (4 calls).

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Rick Astley Never Gonna Give You Up" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Rick Astley Never Gonna Give You Up" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.

steps: Precondition: Chrome is open on any youtube.com page; target the Chrome window via blindly4. The search box may already contain a previous query (e.g. 'Daft Punk Get Lucky'); set-value overwrites it.
Step 1 (find search box): find --title Search --role combobox --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Expect exactly one AXComboBox title="Search". Record its path as SEARCH_BOX.
Step 2 (type query): set-value --path SEARCH_BOX --value "<artist song>" --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.

Step 3 (find submit): find --title Search --role button --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Pick the AXButton whose title is EXACTLY "Search" and whose path = SEARCH_BOX with last index changed from ...0.0.0 to ...0.1 (i.e. the parent's next sibling; it is NOT the 'Clear search query' button at ...0.0.1 and NOT 'Report search predictions'). Ignore other buttons whose title merely contains 'search'.
Step 4 (submit): press --path SEARCH_BUTTON --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 5: wait 2500 ms for results to render.

Step 6 (find result): find --title "<distinctive song title words>" --role link --depth 40 --limit 6 --format xml. Output is usually truncated="true"; that's fine. Take the first AXLink with id="video-title" and value starting https://www.youtube.com/watch (list=RD... radio URLs are acceptable).
Step 7 (play): press --path RESULT_PATH --expect-description "<artist - song title fragment>". Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 8: wait 3000 ms for the watch page to load.

Step 9 (verify): find --title Pause --role button --depth 40 --limit 3 --format xml. Success = AXButton title "Pause (k)". If only 'Play (k)' exists, press it, then re-verify. If neither, wait 3000 ms (ad) and retry once.

Total: 9 calls (3 finds before result, 1 set-value, 1 press submit, 1 find result, 1 press, 1 verify find) plus 2 waits. Paths stay identical within a run, so SEARCH_BOX/SEARCH_BUTTON could be derived from one find, but re-finding the button is the safe default.

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Queen Bohemian Rhapsody" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

blindly4 commands (for reference; you use the actions above):
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Queen Bohemian Rhapsody" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Queen Bohemian Rhapsody" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

Pre-filled search box (e.g. old query): set-value replaces it; no clearing step needed.

Do not reuse paths between runs; layout and tabs change them. Within a run they stay stable, so skip re-finding the button.

steps: Precondition: Chrome is open on any youtube.com page (masthead search visible); target the Chrome window via blindly4. Search box may hold an old query; set-value overwrites it.

Step 1 (find box+button in ONE call): find --title Search --depth 40 --limit 12 --format xml (no role filter). Ignore the omnibox AXTextField 'Address and search bar'. If the output is ambiguous or the button is missing, fall back to two finds: --role combobox --title Search, then --role button --title Search.
Step 2 (type): set-value --path SEARCH_BOX --value "<artist song>" --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.

Step 3 (submit): press --path SEARCH_BUTTON --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}. Within a run SEARCH_BUTTON path = SEARCH_BOX path with the trailing '.0.0' replaced by '.1' (box ...4.0.0.0 -> button ...4.0.1), so no re-find is needed.
Step 4: wait 2500 ms for results to render.

Step 5 (find result): find --title "<distinctive song title words>" --role link --depth 40 --limit 6 --format xml. truncated="true" is normal. Take the first AXLink with id="video-title" and value starting https://www.youtube.com/watch (list=RD... radio URLs are fine). Record RESULT_PATH.
Step 6 (play): press --path RESULT_PATH --expect-description "<title fragment, e.g. Bohemian Rhapsody (Official Video Remastered)>". Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 7: wait 3000 ms.

Step 8 (verify): find --title Pause --role button --depth 40 --limit 3 --format xml. Success = AXButton title 'Pause (k)'. If only 'Play (k)' exists, press it and re-verify. If neither, wait 3000 ms (ad) and retry once.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "a-ha Take On Me" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "a-ha Take On Me" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

steps: Precondition: Chrome open on any youtube.com page with the masthead search visible; target the Chrome window via blindly4. An old query in the box is fine; set-value overwrites it.
Step 1 (find box): find --role combobox --title Search --depth 40 --limit 4 --format xml. Expect exactly one AXComboBox title='Search'. Record SEARCH_BOX path. (Do NOT use --role edit.)

Step 2 (find button): find --role button --title Search --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Choose the AXButton whose title is exactly 'Search' (not 'Clear search query', not 'Search with your voice', not 'Report search predictions'). Record SEARCH_BUTTON. It is the sibling of the box's container: box ...4.0.0.0 -> button ...4.0.1. Optional shortcut: skip this find and derive the path (replace trailing '.0.0' of SEARCH_BOX with '.1'), but the exact-title find is the safe default.
Step 3 (type): set-value --path SEARCH_BOX --value "<artist song>" --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 4 (submit): press --path SEARCH_BUTTON --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 5: wait 2500 ms for results to render.

Step 6 (find result): find --role link --title "<distinctive song title words, e.g. Take On Me>" --depth 40 --limit 6 --format xml. truncated="true" is normal. prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Toto Africa" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Michael Jackson Billie Jean" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

blindly4 commands (for reference; you use the actions above):
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Michael Jackson Billie Jean" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

find --title Search without a role may match the Chrome omnibox ('Address and search bar'). Fix: always give a role (combobox / button) plus title 'Search'.

'Clear search query' button is listed FIRST, right before the real 'Search' button, and pressing it erases the query. --expect-description Search is only a substring check and passes for it too. Fix: pick the button whose title is exactly 'Search'; never first or by index.
'Search with your voice' and 'Report search predictions' also match title Search. Ignore them.
Pre-filled search box (e.g. 'Toto Africa'): set-value replaces it; no clearing step needed.
Find output can be cut off in logs (button list truncated at the third item); the needed 'Search' button appears before the cut. If an element seems missing, raise --limit.
Results show truncated="true" even when fine. Only raise --limit or narrow --title if no AXLink with id=video-title appears.
Result may be a playlist/radio URL (list=RD...&start_radio=1). It still plays the song, so accept it.
The link title includes duration ('... 4 minutes, 56 seconds') but description is the clean title. Use description for --expect-description.
Pressing the result too early fails because results haven't rendered. Wait ~2500 ms after submit.
Always pass --expect-description so a wrong element fails fast.

Over-verification wastes steps: a single Pause (k) find after 3000 ms is conclusive. Last run needlessly waited again, re-found Pause, and searched for 'Skip' (which only returned 'Skip navigation' and a stale ad Skip button). Fix: stop right after the first Pause (k) hit.

Title 'Skip' matches 'Skip navigation' (masthead, offscreen) as well as the ad Skip button (id skip-button:*). A visible Skip button means an ad was showing; press it only if Pause (k) was missing, selecting by id prefix skip-button.

steps: Precondition: Chrome open on any youtube.com page with the masthead search visible; target the Chrome window via blindly4. Any old query in the box is fine; set-value overwrites it.
Step 1 (find box): find --role combobox --title Search --depth 40 --limit 4 --format xml. Expect exactly one AXComboBox title='Search'. Record SEARCH_BOX (path ends ...4.0.0.0).

Step 2 (find button): find --role button --title Search --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Choose the AXButton whose title is exactly 'Search' (path ends ...4.0.1). Never pick 'Clear search query' (listed first), 'Search with your voice', or 'Report search predictions'. Record SEARCH_BUTTON. Sibling rule held in 5 runs: SEARCH_BUTTON = SEARCH_BOX with trailing '.0.0' replaced by '.1'. A program may derive it and skip this find only if press --expect-description Search succeeds and the result check in Step 6 finds a link; otherwise use the exact-title find (safe default).
Step 3 (type): set-value --path SEARCH_BOX --value "<artist song>" --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 4 (submit): press --path SEARCH_BUTTON --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 5: wait 2500 ms for results to render.

Step 6 (find result): find --role link --title "<one distinctive word of the song title, e.g. Billie>" --depth 40 --limit 6 --format xml. Take the first AXLink with id="video-title" and value starting https://www.youtube.com/watch (list=RD... radio URLs are fine). Record RESULT_PATH and its description attribute. truncated="true" is normal.
Step 7 (play): press --path RESULT_PATH --expect-description "<description attribute of that link, e.g. Michael Jackson - Billie Jean (Official Video)>". Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 8: wait 3000 ms.

Step 9 (verify, once): find --role button --title Pause --depth 40 --limit 3 --format xml. One AXButton title 'Pause (k)' means success: stop and report done immediately. Do NOT wait and re-find, and do NOT search for 'Skip' buttons. If only 'Play (k)' appears, press it and re-verify once. If neither appears, wait 3000 ms (ad) and retry once. Only if an ad is suspected (Pause missing or an ad badge), find --role button --title Skip and press the button whose id starts with 'skip-button' (title exactly 'Skip'), never 'Skip navigation'.

Total: 7 tool calls + 2 waits (find box, find button, set-value, press, find result, press, verify). Confirmed on 4 songs (Bohemian Rhapsody, Take On Me, Africa, Billie Jean) with no retries needed. The extra wait, second Pause find and Skip find in the last run were unnecessary; do not repeat them.

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Pharrell Williams Happy" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Pharrell Williams Happy" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

blindly4 commands (for reference; you use the actions above):
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

find --title Search without a role may match the Chrome omnibox ('Address and search bar'). Fix: always give a role plus title 'Search'.

'Clear search query' button is listed FIRST, right before the real 'Search' button, and pressing it erases the query. --expect-description Search is only a substring check and passes for it too. Fix: pick the button whose title is exactly 'Search'; never first or by index.
'Search with your voice' and 'Report search predictions' also match title Search. Ignore them.
Pre-filled search box (e.g. 'Michael Jackson Billie Jean'): set-value replaces it; no clearing step needed.
Find output can be cut off in logs (button list truncated at the third item); the needed 'Search' button appears before the cut. If an element seems missing, raise --limit.

The link title includes duration but description is the clean title. Use description for --expect-description.
Pressing the result too early fails because results haven't rendered. Wait ~2500 ms after submit.
Always pass --expect-description so a wrong element fails fast.

steps: Precondition: Chrome open on any youtube.com page with masthead search visible; target the Chrome window via blindly4. Any old query in the box is fine; set-value overwrites it.

Step 1 (find box + button in one pass): find --role button --title Search --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Pick the AXButton whose title is EXACTLY 'Search' (path ends ...4.0.1). Record SEARCH_BUTTON. Never pick 'Clear search query' (listed first), 'Search with your voice', or 'Report search predictions'.

Step 2 (derive box): SEARCH_BOX = SEARCH_BUTTON with trailing '.1' replaced by '.0.0.0' is NOT correct; use the rule: box path = button path minus trailing '.1' plus '.0.0.0' (e.g. button ...4.0.1 -> box ...4.0.0.0). Held in 6 runs. If a program wants zero risk, run find --role combobox --title Search --depth 40 --limit 4 --format xml and expect exactly one AXComboBox title='Search' (path ends ...4.0.0.0).
Step 3 (type): set-value --path SEARCH_BOX --value "<artist song>" --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 4 (submit): press --path SEARCH_BUTTON --expect-description Search. Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 5: wait 2500 ms for results to render.

Step 6 (find result): find --role link --title "<one distinctive word of the song title, e.g. Happy>" --depth 40 --limit 6 --format xml. Take the first AXLink with id="video-title" and value starting https://www.youtube.com/watch (list=RD... radio URLs are fine). Record RESULT_PATH and its description attribute. truncated="true" is normal.
Step 7 (play): press --path RESULT_PATH --expect-description "<description attribute of that link, e.g. Pharrell Williams - Happy (Official Video)>". Expect {"ok":true}.
Step 8: wait 3000 ms.

Step 9 (verify, once): find --role button --title Pause --depth 40 --limit 3 --format xml. One AXButton title 'Pause (k)' means success: STOP and report done immediately. Do NOT wait and re-find, do NOT query sliders (Seek slider/Volume), do NOT search for Skip. If only 'Play (k)' appears, press it and re-verify once. If neither appears, wait 3000 ms (ad) and retry once. Only if an ad is suspected, find --role button --title Skip and press the button whose id starts with 'skip-button' (title exactly 'Skip'), never 'Skip navigation'.

Total: 7 tool calls + 2 waits (find button, [optional find box], set-value, press, find result, press, verify). Confirmed on 5 songs (Bohemian Rhapsody, Take On Me, Africa, Billie Jean, Happy) with no retries. Last run wasted 6 calls after success (second wait, second Pause find, two slider finds, extra wait); never repeat them.

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Mark Ronson Uptown Funk" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Mark Ronson Uptown Funk" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

steps: Precondition: Chrome open on any youtube.com page with the masthead search visible; target the Chrome window via blindly4. Any existing query is fine because set-value overwrites it.

Step 1 (find button): find --role button --title Search --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Pick the AXButton whose title is EXACTLY 'Search' (path ends ...4.0.1) and record it as SEARCH_BUTTON. Never pick 'Clear search query' (listed first), 'Search with your voice' or 'Report search predictions'.

Step 2 (derive box, no find): SEARCH_BOX = SEARCH_BUTTON minus the trailing '.1', plus '.0.0.0' (…4.0.1 -> …4.0.0.0). Held in 7 runs, including Uptown Funk. Only if step 3 fails, run find --role combobox --title Search --depth 40 --limit 4 --format xml and use the single AXComboBox.
Step 3 (type): set-value --path SEARCH_BOX --value "<artist song>" --expect-description Search. Expect ok:true.
Step 4 (submit): press --path SEARCH_BUTTON --expect-description Search. Expect ok:true.
Step 5: wait 2500 ms for results to render.

Step 6 (find result): find --role link --title "<one distinctive word of the song title>" --depth 40 --limit 6 --format xml. Take the first AXLink with id="video-title" and value starting https://www.youtube.com/watch (list=RD… radio URLs are fine). Record RESULT_PATH and its description. truncated="true" is normal.
Step 7 (play): press --path RESULT_PATH --expect-description "<description, may be a leading prefix such as 'Mark Ronson - Uptown Funk (Official Video) ft. Bruno Mars'>". Expect ok:true.
Step 8: wait 3000 ms.

Step 9 (verify once, then stop): find --role button --title Pause --depth 40 --limit 3 --format xml. One AXButton 'Pause (k)' means success: report done immediately, with no extra waits, re-finds or slider queries. If only 'Play (k)' appears, press it and re-verify once. If neither appears, wait 3000 ms (ad) and retry once. Only if an ad is suspected, find --role button --title Skip and press the button whose id starts with 'skip-button'.

Total: 6 tool calls + 2 waits (find button, set-value, press, find result, press, verify). Confirmed on 6 songs (Bohemian Rhapsody, Take On Me, Africa, Billie Jean, Happy, Uptown Funk) with no retries and no over-verification in the latest run.

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Beyoncé Halo" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

blindly4 commands (for reference; you use the actions above):
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

steps: Precondition: Chrome open on any youtube.com page with the masthead search visible; target the Chrome window via blindly4. Any existing query is fine because set-value overwrites it.

Step 1 (find button): find --role button --title Search --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Pick the AXButton whose title is EXACTLY 'Search' (path ends ...4.0.1) and record it as SEARCH_BUTTON. Never pick 'Clear search query' (listed first, path ends ...4.0.0.1), 'Search with your voice' or 'Report search predictions'.

Step 2 (derive box, no find): SEARCH_BOX = SEARCH_BUTTON minus the trailing '.1', plus '.0.0.0' (…4.0.1 -> …4.0.0.0). Held in 8 runs, including Beyoncé Halo. Only if step 3 fails, run find --role combobox --title Search --depth 40 --limit 4 --format xml and use the single AXComboBox.
Step 3 (type): set-value --path SEARCH_BOX --value "<artist song>" --expect-description Search. Expect ok:true. Non-ASCII characters (é) work.
Step 4 (submit): press --path SEARCH_BUTTON --expect-description Search. Expect ok:true.
Step 5: wait 2500 ms for results to render.

Step 6 (find result): find --role link --title "<one distinctive word of the song title>" --depth 40 --limit 6 --format xml. Take the first AXLink with id="video-title" and value starting https://www.youtube.com/watch (list=RD… radio URLs are fine). Record RESULT_PATH and its description. truncated="true" is normal. In the last run the top result path was 0.1.0.0.1.1.0.1.0.0.5.3.1.0.0.
Step 7 (play): press --path RESULT_PATH --expect-description "<description, may be a leading prefix, e.g. 'Beyoncé - Halo'>". Expect ok:true.
Step 8: wait 3000 ms.

Step 9 (verify ONCE, then stop): find --role button --title Pause --depth 40 --limit 3 --format xml. One AXButton 'Pause (k)' means success: call done IMMEDIATELY. No extra waits, no re-find, no slider queries (the Halo run wasted 2 extra waits and 1 extra find after the first success). If only 'Play (k)' appears, press it and re-verify once. If neither appears, wait 3000 ms (ad) and retry once. Only if an ad is suspected, find --role button --title Skip and press the button whose id starts with 'skip-button'.

Total: 6 tool calls + 2 waits (find button, set-value, press, find result, press, verify), then done. Confirmed on 7 songs (Bohemian Rhapsody, Take On Me, Africa, Billie Jean, Happy, Uptown Funk, Halo). Target for next song: exactly these 8 actions, nothing after the first Pause (k) hit.

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Coldplay Viva La Vida" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

prompt:
You operate Google Chrome on Windows through blindly4, a command-line tool that reads the accessibility (UI Automation) tree of the browser window and triggers UI events. You never run commands yourself: you reply with JSON actions, yuotudidjey runs them through blindly4 (adding the browser's --pid) and shows you the results.

Goal: make YouTube play the song "Coldplay Viva La Vida" — the song itself (an official video or audio, or a normal upload), from its beginning; not a mix, playlist, loop, extended, live or lyrics-only version unless nothing else exists. A separate observer confirms playback; keep acting until it does.

Rules:
- press, set_value and focus need "expect": text contained in the target's accessible name or description; blindly4 checks it before acting, so a stale path fails safely.
- Never touch subscribe, like, share, save, comment, sign-in, purchase or other account or social controls (they are refused).
- Do not close the browser. Keep searches narrow (role, identifier, title, under): listing the whole page is slow.
- Paths are positions in the live tree; they change when the page changes. Find again before acting on a page that may have changed.

Actions (JSON objects, field "cmd" plus its fields):
- {"cmd":"find", "title"|"role"|"value"|"description"|"identifier": text, "under"?: path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — search the tree (case-insensitive contains; identifier exact). Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"list", "under": path, "depth"?: n, "limit"?: n} — every element below a path. Result: XML.
- {"cmd":"inspect", "path": path} — one element in detail.
- {"cmd":"set_value", "path", "value", "expect"} — replace the text of an editable field.
- {"cmd":"press", "path", "expect"} — invoke a button or link.
- {"cmd":"focus", "path", "expect"} — give an element keyboard focus.
- {"cmd":"key", "key": "escape"|"f5"|"0".."9"|"return", "target_path"?, "require_value"?} — return/enter only with target_path + require_value (the focused field must contain exactly that text).
- {"cmd":"scroll", "direction": up|down|left|right, "amount"?: n}
- {"cmd":"hover", "x", "y"} — move the pointer (screen coordinates; an element's frame is x,y,w,h).
- {"cmd":"wait", "ms": up to 5000}
- {"cmd":"done"} — you believe the song is playing.
- {"cmd":"give_up", "reason"}

blindly4 commands (for reference; you use the actions above):
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

find --title Search without a role may match the Chrome omnibox. Fix: always give a role plus title 'Search'.

'Clear search query' is listed FIRST, right before the real 'Search' button, and pressing it erases the query. --expect-description Search is only a substring check and passes for it too. Fix: pick the button whose title is exactly 'Search'; never first or by index.
'Search with your voice' and 'Report search predictions' also match title Search. Ignore them.
Find output in logs can be cut off; the needed 'Search' button appears before the cut. If an element seems missing, raise --limit.
Results show truncated="true" even when fine. Raise --limit or narrow --title only if no AXLink with id=video-title appears.

The link title includes the duration; use the description (clean title, or a prefix) for --expect-description.
