steps: Precondition: Chrome open on any youtube.com page with masthead search visible; target the Chrome window via blindly4. Existing query is fine because set-value overwrites it.

Step 1 (find button): find --role button --title Search --depth 40 --limit 8 --format xml. Pick the AXButton whose title is EXACTLY 'Search' (path ends ...4.0.1, actions AXPress, frame ≈1153,131,80x50) and record it as SEARCH_BUTTON. Never pick 'Clear search query' (listed first, path ends ...4.0.0.1), 'Search with your voice' or 'Report search predictions'.

Step 2 (derive box, no find): SEARCH_BOX = SEARCH_BUTTON minus trailing '.1' plus '.0.0.0' (…4.0.1 -> …4.0.0.0). Held in 9 runs. Only if step 3 fails, run find --role combobox --title Search --depth 40 --limit 4 --format xml and use the single AXComboBox.
Step 3 (type): set-value --path SEARCH_BOX --value "<artist song>" --expect-description Search. Expect ok:true.
Step 4 (submit): press --path SEARCH_BUTTON --expect-description Search. Expect ok:true.
Step 5: wait 2500 ms for results to render.

Step 6 (find result): find --role link --title "<one distinctive ASCII word of the song title>" --depth 40 --limit 6 --format xml. Take the first AXLink with id="video-title" and value starting https://www.youtube.com/watch (list=RD… radio URLs are fine). Record RESULT_PATH and its description. truncated="true" is normal. Top result path has been 0.1.0.0.1.1.0.1.0.0.5.3.1.0.0 for the last two runs.
Step 7 (play): press --path RESULT_PATH --expect-description "<description or leading prefix, e.g. 'Coldplay - Viva La Vida (Official Video)'>". Expect ok:true.
Step 8: wait 3000 ms.

Step 9 (verify ONCE, then STOP): find --role button --title Pause --depth 40 --limit 3 --format xml. One AXButton 'Pause (k)' = success: call done IMMEDIATELY and end the task. Do NOT wait, re-find Pause, search for Skip, or press anything afterwards (the Viva La Vida run wasted ~10 extra actions after the first Pause hit, including pressing 'Skip navigation'). If only 'Play (k)' appears, press it and re-verify once. If neither appears, wait 3000 ms (ad) and retry once. Only if Pause is still absent and an ad is suspected, find --role button --title Skip --limit 4 and press the button whose id starts with 'skip-button'.

Confirmed on 8 songs (Bohemian Rhapsody, Take On Me, Africa, Billie Jean, Happy, Uptown Funk, Halo, Viva La Vida). prompt:
Write solution.py: a standalone Python 3.13 program (standard library only) that plays a list of YouTube songs in an already-open Google Chrome using only blindly4 — no LLM, no network access of its own.

Command line: --songs FILE (UTF-8, one search query per line; skip blank lines and lines starting with #), --max-songs N (stop after N songs; without it, play forever), --forever (explicit forever), --start-index N (first list position, default 0), --max-play-seconds S (testing only: pause S seconds after playback starts if that comes first).

Behaviour, per song, looping over the list forever (itertools.cycle):
1. Emit song_assigned BEFORE any blindly4 call for that song.
2. Search YouTube for the query and open the right video: the song itself (official video/audio or a normal upload), not a mix, playlist, Short, live stream or loop.
3. Make sure it plays from its beginning; emit playback_started when you see it playing (include "position" if known).
4. Wait until 3 seconds before the end of the video, then pause it; emit paused with "duration" (video length in seconds you used) and "remaining" (seconds left by your computation).
5. Then the next song. If a song cannot be found or played after a few retries, emit step_error with a "reason" and continue with the next song.
Exit with status 0 after --max-songs songs.

The browser: Chrome is already open on YouTube; its process id is in the environment variable YUO_CHROME_PID. Never open or close the browser.
blindly4: call it ONLY through the command prefix in the environment variable YUO_B4 (a JSON array of strings): subprocess.run([*prefix, *args], capture_output=True) with args a blindly4 argument list that includes "--pid", pid. Decode stdout/stderr as UTF-8. stdout is JSON (XML with --format xml). Exit codes: 0 ok, 64 usage error or refused by the safety guard, 77 accessibility error (target gone, not foreground, ...).
Every call except apps and schema must include --pid with the YUO_CHROME_PID value; the proxy refuses calls aimed at any other window.
The proxy refuses: type, click, paste; press/set-value/focus without --expect-description; labels that start with, or are fragments of, subscribe, like, dislike, share, save, join, comment, reply, report, sign in, buy, premium, download, thanks, clip, remix, notify, create, upload; keys other than escape, f5, a digit, or return/enter given with --target-path and --require-value.
Keyboard and pointer input (key, hover, scroll) need Chrome in the foreground: run "activate" first when needed.
Tree paths change whenever the page changes: find an element again right before acting on it; when reusing a remembered path, check it first and fall back to find.
Read-only lookups may run concurrently (concurrent.futures; the first successful result wins); input commands must run one at a time.

Events: append one JSON object per line to the file named in the environment variable YUO_EVENTS (UTF-8; open, append, close each time):
{"t": time.time(), "stage": "exploitation", "source": "solution", "kind": KIND, "song_index": list position, "song": query, ...extra fields}
KIND is one of song_assigned, playback_started, paused, ad_seen, step_error.

Style — functional programming (checked by a linter; violations are rejected):
- Pure functions for parsing, matching and decisions; side effects (blindly4 calls, clock, sleep, event writes) confined to a small, clearly named set of effect functions.
- Immutable data only: @dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple, tuples, frozenset. No mutable globals.
- Use lambdas (at least 5), map/filter, functools.reduce, functools.partial, itertools (cycle, islice, repeat, takewhile, dropwhile, count), and a compose/pipe helper.
- Forbidden: while loops (iterate lazily: e.g. next(filter(ready, map(probe, itertools.repeat(None))))), global, nonlocal, augmented assignment (+= etc.), del, item or attribute assignment, mutating methods (append, extend, insert, pop, remove, clear, update, setdefault, popitem, add, discard, sort, reverse), classes other than frozen dataclasses / NamedTuple / Enum.
- Forbidden imports: anthropic, openai, requests, urllib, http, socket, httpx, aiohttp, ctypes, comtypes, pywinauto, uiautomation, win32*, selenium, playwright, webbrowser, asyncio, importlib, multiprocessing, ssl and other network modules; no __import__/eval/exec/compile; no os.system/os.popen/os.startfile/os.spawn*/os.exec*; no string mentioning claude, codex or blindly4.exe.
- Every subprocess call is a direct call (not via partial or an alias) whose command is exactly [*prefix, *args] with prefix = the YUO_B4 array used whole — never index or slice it.


How the exploration stage's timer paused each song (its calls appear in the trace with origin "driver"):
- Right after playback was confirmed it hovered the pointer over the centre of the YouTube player ("hover" with the player element's frame centre) and then read the player's seek slider; the slider's value text ("X Minutes Y Seconds of A Minutes B Seconds") is only up to date right after such a hover — without it the text can be stale, even showing a finished ad.
- It computed start = now − position and deadline = start + duration − 3 s − 0.6 s (the pause call's own latency), slept until 15 s before the deadline, hovered and read again to re-sync, slept until the deadline, then pressed the pause control.
- Even right after a hover the text is sometimes stale, so a reading was believed only if its duration matched and the start it implied (now − position) was within 10 s of the start already known (the moment playback was first seen); otherwise the earlier estimate was kept. Hover by moving across the player (e.g. 40 px left of its centre, then the centre) and wait about 0.8 s before reading.

blindly4 commands available through YUO_B4:
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

Write solution.py: a standalone Python 3.13 program (standard library only) that plays a list of YouTube songs in an already-open Google Chrome using only blindly4 — no LLM, no network access of its own.

Command line: --songs FILE (UTF-8, one search query per line; skip blank lines and lines starting with #), --max-songs N (stop after N songs; without it, play forever), --forever (explicit forever), --start-index N (first list position, default 0), --max-play-seconds S (testing only: pause S seconds after playback starts if that comes first).

Behaviour, per song, looping over the list forever (itertools.cycle):
1. Emit song_assigned BEFORE any blindly4 call for that song.
2. Search YouTube for the query and open the right video: the song itself (official video/audio or a normal upload), not a mix, playlist, Short, live stream or loop.
3. Make sure it plays from its beginning; emit playback_started when you see it playing (include "position" if known).
4. Wait until 3 seconds before the end of the video, then pause it; emit paused with "duration" (video length in seconds you used) and "remaining" (seconds left by your computation).
5. Then the next song. If a song cannot be found or played after a few retries, emit step_error with a "reason" and continue with the next song.
Exit with status 0 after --max-songs songs.

The browser: Chrome is already open on YouTube; its process id is in the environment variable YUO_CHROME_PID. Never open or close the browser.
blindly4: call it ONLY through the command prefix in the environment variable YUO_B4 (a JSON array of strings): subprocess.run([*prefix, *args], capture_output=True) with args a blindly4 argument list that includes "--pid", pid. Decode stdout/stderr as UTF-8. stdout is JSON (XML with --format xml). Exit codes: 0 ok, 64 usage error or refused by the safety guard, 77 accessibility error (target gone, not foreground, ...).
Every call except apps and schema must include --pid with the YUO_CHROME_PID value; the proxy refuses calls aimed at any other window.
The proxy refuses: type, click, paste; press/set-value/focus without --expect-description; labels that start with, or are fragments of, subscribe, like, dislike, share, save, join, comment, reply, report, sign in, buy, premium, download, thanks, clip, remix, notify, create, upload; keys other than escape, f5, a digit, or return/enter given with --target-path and --require-value.
Keyboard and pointer input (key, hover, scroll) need Chrome in the foreground: run "activate" first when needed.
Tree paths change whenever the page changes: find an element again right before acting on it; when reusing a remembered path, check it first and fall back to find.
Read-only lookups may run concurrently (concurrent.futures; the first successful result wins); input commands must run one at a time.

Events: append one JSON object per line to the file named in the environment variable YUO_EVENTS (UTF-8; open, append, close each time):
{"t": time.time(), "stage": "exploitation", "source": "solution", "kind": KIND, "song_index": list position, "song": query, ...extra fields}
KIND is one of song_assigned, playback_started, paused, ad_seen, step_error.

Style — functional programming (checked by a linter; violations are rejected):
- Pure functions for parsing, matching and decisions; side effects (blindly4 calls, clock, sleep, event writes) confined to a small, clearly named set of effect functions.
- Immutable data only: @dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple, tuples, frozenset. No mutable globals.
- Use lambdas (at least 5), map/filter, functools.reduce, functools.partial, itertools (cycle, islice, repeat, takewhile, dropwhile, count), and a compose/pipe helper.
- Forbidden: while loops (iterate lazily: e.g. next(filter(ready, map(probe, itertools.repeat(None))))), global, nonlocal, augmented assignment (+= etc.), del, item or attribute assignment, mutating methods (append, extend, insert, pop, remove, clear, update, setdefault, popitem, add, discard, sort, reverse), classes other than frozen dataclasses / NamedTuple / Enum.
- Forbidden imports: anthropic, openai, requests, urllib, http, socket, httpx, aiohttp, ctypes, comtypes, pywinauto, uiautomation, win32*, selenium, playwright, webbrowser, asyncio, importlib, multiprocessing, ssl and other network modules; no __import__/eval/exec/compile; no os.system/os.popen/os.startfile/os.spawn*/os.exec*; no string mentioning claude, codex or blindly4.exe.
- Every subprocess call is a direct call (not via partial or an alias) whose command is exactly [*prefix, *args] with prefix = the YUO_B4 array used whole — never index or slice it.


How the exploration stage's timer paused each song (its calls appear in the trace with origin "driver"):
- Right after playback was confirmed it hovered the pointer over the centre of the YouTube player ("hover" with the player element's frame centre) and then read the player's seek slider; the slider's value text ("X Minutes Y Seconds of A Minutes B Seconds") is only up to date right after such a hover — without it the text can be stale, even showing a finished ad.
- It computed start = now − position and deadline = start + duration − 3 s − 0.6 s (the pause call's own latency), slept until 15 s before the deadline, hovered and read again to re-sync, slept until the deadline, then pressed the pause control.
- Even right after a hover the text is sometimes stale, so a reading was believed only if its duration matched and the start it implied (now − position) was within 10 s of the start already known (the moment playback was first seen); otherwise the earlier estimate was kept. Hover by moving across the player (e.g. 40 px left of its centre, then the centre) and wait about 0.8 s before reading.

blindly4 commands available through YUO_B4:
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

compose = lambda *fns: (lambda x: functools.reduce(lambda acc, f: f(acc), fns, x))
pipe = lambda x, *fns: compose(*fns)(x)


def first_where(pred, items):
    return next(itertools.dropwhile(lambda x: not pred(x), items), None)


def tokens(text):

# Pure parsing / decisions
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

keep_line = lambda line: bool(line) and not line.startswith("#")
parse_songs = compose(str.splitlines, functools.partial(map, str.strip),

        return json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        return None

    data = parse_json(result.out) if result.code == 0 else None
    return tuple(m for m in data.get("matches", ()) if isinstance(m, dict)) if isinstance(data, dict) else ()


def phrase_seconds(text):
    parts = re.findall(r"(\d+)\s*(hour|minute|second)", text.casefold())
    units = dict(UNIT_SECONDS)
    return sum(int(n) * units[u] for n, u in parts) if parts else None


def title_duration(title):
    found = DURATION_RE.search(title.strip())
    return phrase_seconds(found.group(1)) if found else None


def find_args(title=None, role=None, identifier=None, limit=8, fmt=None):
    pairs = (("--title", title), ("--role", role), ("--identifier", identifier))
    flags = tuple(itertools.chain.from_iterable((k, v) for k, v in pairs if v))
    tail = ("--format", fmt) if fmt else ()
    return ("find", *flags, "--depth", "40", "--limit", str(limit), *tail)

keep_line = lambda line: bool(line) and not line.startswith("#")

def parse_json(text):

    data = parse_json(result.out) if result.code == 0 else None
    return tuple(m for m in data.get("matches", ()) if isinstance(m, dict)) if isinstance(data, dict) else ()


def phrase_seconds(text):
    parts = re.findall(r"(\d+)\s*(hour|minute|second)", text.casefold())
    units = dict(UNIT_SECONDS)
    return sum(int(n) * units[u] for n, u in parts) if parts else None


def title_duration(title):
    found = DURATION_RE.search(title.strip())
    return phrase_seconds(found.group(1)) if found else None


def find_args(title=None, role=None, identifier=None, limit=8, fmt=None):
    pairs = (("--title", title), ("--role", role), ("--identifier", identifier))
    flags = tuple(itertools.chain.from_iterable((k, v) for k, v in pairs if v))
    tail = ("--format", fmt) if fmt else ()
    return ("find", *flags, "--depth", "40", "--limit", str(limit), *tail)

        return (), "search button not found"
    box_path = box["path"] if box else derive_box(button["path"])
    typed = b4(cfg, "set-value", "--path", box_path, "--value", song.query, "--expect-description", "Search")
    if typed.code != 0:
        return (), "set-value failed: " + typed.err.strip()[:120]
    sent = b4(cfg, "press", "--path", button["path"], "--expect-description", "Search")
    if sent.code != 0:
        return (), "search press failed: " + sent.err.strip()[:120]
    nap(2.5)
    found = poll(lambda: rank_results(
        song.query, find_matches(cfg, role="link", identifier="video-title", limit=12)), 4, 1.5)
    return (found or ()), ("" if found else "no suitable result")


def acquire_step(cfg, song, acc, i):
    if acc.done:
        return acc
    pause, skip, play = concurrently(
        lambda t: find_matches(cfg, title=t, role="button", limit=6), ("Pause", "Skip", "Play"))
    state, target = classify(pause, skip, play)
    if state == "playing":
        return Acq(True, acc.ad_seen, now())
    if state == "ad":
        if not acc.ad_seen:
            emit(cfg, song, "ad_seen")
        b4(cfg, "press", "--path", target["path"], "--expect-description", target.get("description") or "Skip")
        nap(1.5)
        return acc._replace(ad_seen=True)
    if state == "paused" and i >= 3:
        b4(cfg, "press", "--path", target["path"], "--expect-description", target.get("description") or "Play")
    nap(1.5 if state == "paused" else 2.0)
    return acc


def play_candidate(cfg, song, cand):
    opened = b4(cfg, "press", "--path", cand.path, "--expect-description", cand.description)
    if opened.code != 0:
        return Outcome(False, "open failed (%d): %s" % (opened.code, opened.err.strip()[:120]), True)
    nap(3.0)
    acq = functools.reduce(functools.partial(acquire_step, cfg, song), range(12), Acq(False, False, now()))
    if not acq.done:
        return Outcome(False, "playback not confirmed", True)
    reading = poll(functools.partial(confirm, cfg, cand.duration), 5, 1.0)
    start = implied_start(reading) if reading else acq.t_seen
    duration = reading.duration if reading else cand.duration
    started_at = now()
    emit(cfg, song, "playback_started", title=cand.description,
         **({"position": reading.position} if reading else {}))
    natural = pause_deadline(start, duration)
    deadline = natural if cfg.max_play is None else min(natural, started_at + cfg.max_play)
    capped = deadline < natural - 0.001
    resync_at = deadline - RESYNC_LEAD
    start = start if capped or resync_at - now() < 2 else (
        nap_until(resync_at) or refine_start(start, sync(cfg), duration))
    deadline = deadline if capped else pause_deadline(start, duration)
    pressed = pause_video(cfg, deadline)
    if pressed.code != 0:
        return Outcome(False, "pause failed (%d): %s" % (pressed.code, pressed.err.strip()[:120]), False)
    remaining = duration - (now() - start)
    emit(cfg, song, "paused", duration=duration, remaining=round(remaining, 2))
    return Outcome(True, "", False)


def attempt_song(cfg, song, attempt):
    cands, reason = search_candidates(cfg, song)
    if not cands:
        return Outcome(False, reason or "no candidates", True)
    return play_candidate(cfg, song, cands[attempt % len(cands)])


def play_song(cfg, song):
    emit(cfg, song, "song_assigned")
    outcome = functools.reduce(
        lambda prev, i: prev if (prev.ok or not prev.retry) else attempt_song(cfg, song, i),
        range(3), Outcome(False, "not attempted", True))
    return outcome if outcome.ok else (emit(cfg, song, "step_error", reason=outcome.reason) or outcome)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Entry point
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def parse_args(argv):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--songs", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--max-songs", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--forever", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--start-index", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--max-play-seconds", type=float, default=None)
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def load_config(args):
    return Config(
        pid=os.environ["YUO_CHROME_PID"],
        events=os.environ["YUO_EVENTS"],
        max_play=args.max_play_seconds,
    )


def main(argv):
    args = parse_args(argv)
    cfg = load_config(args)
    songs = tuple(itertools.starmap(Song, enumerate(parse_songs(read_text(args.songs)))))
    if not songs:
        sys.stderr.write("no songs in list\n")
        return 2
    stream = itertools.islice(itertools.cycle(songs), args.start_index % len(songs), None)
    limit = None if args.forever or args.max_songs is None else max(0, args.max_songs)
    limited = stream if limit is None else itertools.islice(stream, limit)
    collections.deque(map(play_song, itertools.repeat(cfg), limited), maxlen=0)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

Write solution.py: a standalone Python 3.13 program (standard library only) that plays a list of YouTube songs in an already-open Google Chrome using only blindly4 — no LLM, no network access of its own.

Command line: --songs FILE (UTF-8, one search query per line; skip blank lines and lines starting with #), --max-songs N (stop after N songs; without it, play forever), --forever (explicit forever), --start-index N (first list position, default 0), --max-play-seconds S (testing only: pause S seconds after playback starts if that comes first).

Behaviour, per song, looping over the list forever (itertools.cycle):
1. Emit song_assigned BEFORE any blindly4 call for that song.
2. Search YouTube for the query and open the right video: the song itself (official video/audio or a normal upload), not a mix, playlist, Short, live stream or loop.
3. Make sure it plays from its beginning; emit playback_started when you see it playing (include "position" if known).
4. Wait until 3 seconds before the end of the video, then pause it; emit paused with "duration" (video length in seconds you used) and "remaining" (seconds left by your computation).
5. Then the next song. If a song cannot be found or played after a few retries, emit step_error with a "reason" and continue with the next song.
Exit with status 0 after --max-songs songs.

The browser: Chrome is already open on YouTube; its process id is in the environment variable YUO_CHROME_PID. Never open or close the browser.
blindly4: call it ONLY through the command prefix in the environment variable YUO_B4 (a JSON array of strings): subprocess.run([*prefix, *args], capture_output=True) with args a blindly4 argument list that includes "--pid", pid. Decode stdout/stderr as UTF-8. stdout is JSON (XML with --format xml). Exit codes: 0 ok, 64 usage error or refused by the safety guard, 77 accessibility error (target gone, not foreground, ...).
Every call except apps and schema must include --pid with the YUO_CHROME_PID value; the proxy refuses calls aimed at any other window.
The proxy refuses: type, click, paste; press/set-value/focus without --expect-description; labels that start with, or are fragments of, subscribe, like, dislike, share, save, join, comment, reply, report, sign in, buy, premium, download, thanks, clip, remix, notify, create, upload; keys other than escape, f5, a digit, or return/enter given with --target-path and --require-value.
Keyboard and pointer input (key, hover, scroll) need Chrome in the foreground: run "activate" first when needed.
Tree paths change whenever the page changes: find an element again right before acting on it; when reusing a remembered path, check it first and fall back to find.
Read-only lookups may run concurrently (concurrent.futures; the first successful result wins); input commands must run one at a time.

Events: append one JSON object per line to the file named in the environment variable YUO_EVENTS (UTF-8; open, append, close each time):
{"t": time.time(), "stage": "exploitation", "source": "solution", "kind": KIND, "song_index": list position, "song": query, ...extra fields}
KIND is one of song_assigned, playback_started, paused, ad_seen, step_error.

Style — functional programming (checked by a linter; violations are rejected):
- Pure functions for parsing, matching and decisions; side effects (blindly4 calls, clock, sleep, event writes) confined to a small, clearly named set of effect functions.
- Immutable data only: @dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple, tuples, frozenset. No mutable globals.
- Use lambdas (at least 5), map/filter, functools.reduce, functools.partial, itertools (cycle, islice, repeat, takewhile, dropwhile, count), and a compose/pipe helper.
- Forbidden: while loops (iterate lazily: e.g. next(filter(ready, map(probe, itertools.repeat(None))))), global, nonlocal, augmented assignment (+= etc.), del, item or attribute assignment, mutating methods (append, extend, insert, pop, remove, clear, update, setdefault, popitem, add, discard, sort, reverse), classes other than frozen dataclasses / NamedTuple / Enum.
- Forbidden imports: anthropic, openai, requests, urllib, http, socket, httpx, aiohttp, ctypes, _ctypes, cffi, comtypes, pywinauto, uiautomation, win32*, pythoncom, pywintypes, _winapi, nt, posix, pyautogui, pynput, keyboard, mouse, selenium, playwright, webbrowser, asyncio, importlib, multiprocessing, ssl and other network modules; no __import__/eval/exec/compile/globals/locals/vars, no dunder names or attributes (__dict__, __builtins__, ...) other than __name__, no sys.modules; no os.system/os.popen/os.startfile/os.spawn*/os.exec*; no string mentioning claude, codex or blindly4.exe.
- Every subprocess call is a direct call (not via partial or an alias) whose command is exactly [*prefix, *args], where prefix = json.loads(os.environ["YUO_B4"]) is a name bound nowhere else (not a parameter, not a loop variable, not assigned anything else) and is used whole — never index or slice it. Use the subprocess and os modules only as subprocess.<name> / os.<name>, never as values.


How the exploration stage's own code decided that the song itself was playing and timed the pause (its calls appear in the trace with origin "driver" or "observer"):
- Ads: an ad is running while the player (the element with identifier movie_player; search inside it with find --under <its path> --depth 5) contains an element titled exactly "Sponsored", "My Ad Center", "Skip", "Skip Ad" or "Skip Ads". Unskippable ads show a Pause (k) button and no Skip button, so a Pause (k) button alone does not mean the song is playing: it is playing when Pause (k) is shown and no ad marker is. Short bumper ads (about 5 s) show no marker at all, and after an ad YouTube can take several more seconds to load the song.
- Right after playback was confirmed it hovered the pointer over the centre of the YouTube player ("hover" with the player element's frame centre) and then read the player's seek slider; the slider's value text ("X Minutes Y Seconds of A Minutes B Seconds") is only up to date right after such a hover — without it the text can be stale, even showing a finished ad.
- It computed start = now − position and deadline = start + duration − 3 s − 0.6 s (the pause call's own latency), slept until 15 s before the deadline, hovered and read again to re-sync, slept until the deadline, then pressed the pause control.
- Even right after a hover the text is sometimes stale, so a reading was believed for the start only if it was song-length (duration at least 60 s and within 3 s of the video's length) and the start it implied (now − position) lay between 10 s before and 60 s after the moment the song was first seen playing with no ad marker. Until a reading was believed it kept taking readings, about every 2–5 s, up to 40 tries. Hover by moving across the player (e.g. 40 px left of its centre, then the centre) and wait about 0.8 s before reading.
- The re-sync reading 15 s before the deadline moved the pause only if its duration matched and the start it implied agreed with the start in use within 10 s; otherwise the earlier estimate was kept.

Write solution.py: a standalone Python 3.13 program (standard library only) that plays a list of YouTube songs in an already-open Google Chrome using only blindly4 — no LLM, no network access of its own.

Command line: --songs FILE (UTF-8, one search query per line; skip blank lines and lines starting with #), --max-songs N (stop after N songs; without it, play forever), --forever (explicit forever), --start-index N (first list position, default 0), --max-play-seconds S (testing only: pause S seconds after playback starts if that comes first).

Behaviour, per song, looping over the list forever (itertools.cycle):
1. Emit song_assigned BEFORE any blindly4 call for that song.
2. Search YouTube for the query and open the right video: the song itself (official video/audio or a normal upload), not a mix, playlist, Short, live stream or loop.
3. Make sure it plays from its beginning; emit playback_started when you see it playing (include "position" if known).
4. Wait until 3 seconds before the end of the video, then pause it; emit paused with "duration" (video length in seconds you used) and "remaining" (seconds left by your computation).
5. Then the next song. If a song cannot be found or played after a few retries, emit step_error with a "reason" and continue with the next song.
Exit with status 0 after --max-songs songs.

The browser: Chrome is already open on YouTube; its process id is in the environment variable YUO_CHROME_PID. Never open or close the browser.
blindly4: call it ONLY through the command prefix in the environment variable YUO_B4 (a JSON array of strings): subprocess.run([*prefix, *args], capture_output=True) with args a blindly4 argument list that includes "--pid", pid. Decode stdout/stderr as UTF-8. stdout is JSON (XML with --format xml). Exit codes: 0 ok, 64 usage error or refused by the safety guard, 77 accessibility error (target gone, not foreground, ...).
Every call except apps and schema must include --pid with the YUO_CHROME_PID value; the proxy refuses calls aimed at any other window.
The proxy refuses: type, click, paste; press/set-value/focus without --expect-description; labels that start with, or are fragments of, subscribe, like, dislike, share, save, join, comment, reply, report, sign in, buy, premium, download, thanks, clip, remix, notify, create, upload; keys other than escape, f5, a digit, or return/enter given with --target-path and --require-value.
Keyboard and pointer input (key, hover, scroll) need Chrome in the foreground: run "activate" first when needed.
Tree paths change whenever the page changes: find an element again right before acting on it; when reusing a remembered path, check it first and fall back to find.
Read-only lookups may run concurrently (concurrent.futures; the first successful result wins); input commands must run one at a time.

Events: append one JSON object per line to the file named in the environment variable YUO_EVENTS (UTF-8; open, append, close each time):
{"t": time.time(), "stage": "exploitation", "source": "solution", "kind": KIND, "song_index": list position, "song": query, ...extra fields}
KIND is one of song_assigned, playback_started, paused, ad_seen, step_error.

Style — functional programming (checked by a linter; violations are rejected):
- Pure functions for parsing, matching and decisions; side effects (blindly4 calls, clock, sleep, event writes) confined to a small, clearly named set of effect functions.
- Immutable data only: @dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple, tuples, frozenset. No mutable globals.
- Use lambdas (at least 5), map/filter, functools.reduce, functools.partial, itertools (cycle, islice, repeat, takewhile, dropwhile, count), and a compose/pipe helper.
- Forbidden: while loops (iterate lazily: e.g. next(filter(ready, map(probe, itertools.repeat(None))))), global, nonlocal, augmented assignment (+= etc.), del, item or attribute assignment, mutating methods (append, extend, insert, pop, remove, clear, update, setdefault, popitem, add, discard, sort, reverse), classes other than frozen dataclasses / NamedTuple / Enum.
- Forbidden imports: anthropic, openai, requests, urllib, http, socket, httpx, aiohttp, ctypes, _ctypes, cffi, comtypes, pywinauto, uiautomation, win32*, pythoncom, pywintypes, _winapi, nt, posix, pyautogui, pynput, keyboard, mouse, selenium, playwright, webbrowser, asyncio, importlib, multiprocessing, ssl and other network modules; no __import__/eval/exec/compile/globals/locals/vars, no dunder names or attributes (__dict__, __builtins__, ...) other than __name__, no sys.modules; no os.system/os.popen/os.startfile/os.spawn*/os.exec*; no string mentioning claude, codex or blindly4.exe.
- Every subprocess call is a direct call (not via partial or an alias) whose command is exactly [*prefix, *args], where prefix = json.loads(os.environ["YUO_B4"]) is a name bound nowhere else (not a parameter, not a loop variable, not assigned anything else) and is used whole — never index or slice it. Use the subprocess and os modules only as subprocess.<name> / os.<name>, never as values.


How the exploration stage's own code decided that the song itself was playing and timed the pause (its calls appear in the trace with origin "driver" or "observer"):
- Ads: an ad is running while the player (the element with identifier movie_player; search inside it with find --under <its path> --depth 5) contains an element titled exactly "Sponsored", "My Ad Center", "Skip", "Skip Ad" or "Skip Ads". Unskippable ads show a Pause (k) button and no Skip button, so a Pause (k) button alone does not mean the song is playing: it is playing when Pause (k) is shown and no ad marker is. Short bumper ads (about 5 s) show no marker at all, and after an ad YouTube can take several more seconds to load the song.
- Right after playback was confirmed it hovered the pointer over the centre of the YouTube player ("hover" with the player element's frame centre) and then read the player's seek slider; the slider's value text ("X Minutes Y Seconds of A Minutes B Seconds") is only up to date right after such a hover — without it the text can be stale, even showing a finished ad.
- It computed start = now − position and deadline = start + duration − 3 s − 0.6 s (the pause call's own latency), slept until 15 s before the deadline, hovered and read again to re-sync, slept until the deadline, then pressed the pause control.
- Even right after a hover the text is sometimes stale, so a reading was believed for the start only if it was song-length (duration at least 60 s and within 3 s of the video's length) and the start it implied (now − position) lay between 10 s before and 60 s after the moment the song was first seen playing with no ad marker. Until a reading was believed it kept taking readings, about every 2–5 s, up to 40 tries. Hover by moving across the player (e.g. 40 px left of its centre, then the centre) and wait about 0.8 s before reading.
- The re-sync reading 15 s before the deadline moved the pause only if its duration matched and the start it implied agreed with the start in use within 10 s; otherwise the earlier estimate was kept.

blindly4 commands available through YUO_B4:
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

Write solution.py: a standalone Python 3.13 program (standard library only) that plays a list of YouTube songs in an already-open Google Chrome using only blindly4 — no LLM, no network access of its own.

Command line: --songs FILE (UTF-8, one search query per line; skip blank lines and lines starting with #), --max-songs N (stop after N songs; without it, play forever), --forever (explicit forever), --start-index N (first list position, default 0), --max-play-seconds S (testing only: pause S seconds after playback starts if that comes first).

Behaviour, per song, looping over the list forever (itertools.cycle):
1. Emit song_assigned BEFORE any blindly4 call for that song.
2. Search YouTube for the query and open the right video: the song itself (official video/audio or a normal upload), not a mix, playlist, Short, live stream or loop.
3. Make sure it plays from its beginning; emit playback_started when you see it playing (include "position" if known).
4. Wait until 3 seconds before the end of the video, then pause it; emit paused with "duration" (video length in seconds you used) and "remaining" (seconds left by your computation).
5. Then the next song. If a song cannot be found or played after a few retries, emit step_error with a "reason" and continue with the next song.
Exit with status 0 after --max-songs songs.

Every call except apps and schema must include --pid with the YUO_CHROME_PID value; the proxy refuses calls aimed at any other window.
The proxy refuses: type, click, paste; press/set-value/focus without --expect-description; labels that start with, or are fragments of, subscribe, like, dislike, share, save, join, comment, reply, report, sign in, buy, premium, download, thanks, clip, remix, notify, create, upload; keys other than escape, f5, a digit, or return/enter given with --target-path and --require-value.

Tree paths change whenever the page changes: find an element again right before acting on it; when reusing a remembered path, check it first and fall back to find.

How the exploration stage's own code decided that the song itself was playing and timed the pause (its calls appear in the trace with origin "driver" or "observer"):
- Ads: an ad is running while the player (the element with identifier movie_player; search inside it with find --under <its path> --depth 5) contains an element titled exactly "Sponsored", "My Ad Center", "Skip", "Skip Ad" or "Skip Ads". Unskippable ads show a Pause (k) button and no Skip button, so a Pause (k) button alone does not mean the song is playing: it is playing when Pause (k) is shown and no ad marker is. Short bumper ads (about 5 s) show no marker at all, and after an ad YouTube can take several more seconds to load the song.
- Right after playback was confirmed it hovered the pointer over the centre of the YouTube player ("hover" with the player element's frame centre) and then read the player's seek slider; the slider's value text ("X Minutes Y Seconds of A Minutes B Seconds") is only up to date right after such a hover — without it the text can be stale, even showing a finished ad.
- It computed start = now − position and deadline = start + duration − 3 s − 0.6 s (the pause call's own latency), slept until 15 s before the deadline, hovered and read again to re-sync, slept until the deadline, then pressed the pause control.
- Even right after a hover the text is sometimes stale, so a reading was believed for the start only if it was song-length (duration at least 60 s and within 3 s of the video's length) and the start it implied (now − position) lay between 10 s before and 60 s after the moment the song was first seen playing with no ad marker. Until a reading was believed it kept taking readings, about every 2–5 s, up to 40 tries. Hover by moving across the player (e.g. 40 px left of its centre, then the centre) and wait about 0.8 s before reading.
- The re-sync reading 15 s before the deadline moved the pause only if its duration matched and the start it implied agreed with the start in use within 10 s; otherwise the earlier estimate was kept.

blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]

The exploration stage's playbook (written by the LLM that drove the browser):
{"pitfalls":["find --role edit for 'Search' returns empty: YouTube's search box is an AXComboBox. Fix: use --role combobox (only needed as a fallback).","find --title Search without a role may match the Chrome omnibox. Fix: always give a role plus title 'Search'.","'Clear search query' is listed FIRST, right before the real 'Search' button, and pressing it erases the query. --expect-description Search is only a substring check and passes for it too. Fix: pick the button whose title is exactly 'Search'; never first or by index.","'Search with your voice' and 'Report search predictions' also match title Search. Ignore them.","Find output in logs can be cut off; the needed 'Search' button appears before the cut. If an element seems missing, raise --limit.","Results show truncated=\"true\" even when fine. It still plays the song, so accept it.","The link title includes the duration; use the description (clean title, or a prefix) for --expect-description.","Pressing the result too early fails because results haven't rendered. Wait ~2500 ms after submit.","Always pass --expect-description so a wrong element fails fast.","OVER-VERIFICATION (recurred in Halo AND Viva La Vida: after the first Pause (k) hit and done, the run waited 2000 ms, re-found Pause, searched Skip, pressed 'Skip navigation' and then the ad Skip button, ~10 wasted actions). If only 'Play (k)' appears, press it and re-verify once. If neither appears, wait 3000 ms (ad) and retry once. keep_line = lambda line: bool(line) and not line.startswith("#")
parse_songs = compose(str.splitlines, partial(map, str.strip), partial(filter, keep_line), tuple)


def safe_json(text):
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def elem_from(role, d):
    g = lambda k: str(d.get(k) or "")
    return Elem(role, g("path"), g("title"), g("description"),
                g("identifier") or g("id"), g("value"), g("frame"))


def parse_json_matches(text):
    data = safe_json(text)
    items = data.get("matches", ()) if isinstance(data, dict) else ()
    return tuple(map(lambda m: elem_from(str(m.get("role", "")), m),
                     filter(lambda m: isinstance(m, dict), items)))


def parse_xml(text):
    attrs = lambda raw: dict(map(lambda a: (a[0], html.unescape(a[1])), ATTR_RE.findall(raw)))
    return tuple(map(lambda m: elem_from(m.group(1), attrs(m.group(2))), TAG_RE.finditer(text)))


def elems_of(res, xml=False):
    if res.code != 0:
        return ()
    return parse_xml(res.out) if xml else parse_json_matches(res.out)


def duration_from_title(title):
    parts = tuple(itertools.chain.from_iterable(map(
        lambda unit: tuple(map(lambda n: int(n) * unit[1], unit[0].findall(title)[-1:])),
        DURATION_UNITS)))
    return sum(parts) if parts else None


def words(text):
    return frozenset(re.findall(r"[\w']+", text.lower()))


def acceptable(query, e):
    length = duration_from_title(e.title)
    banned = (words(e.title) & BANNED_WORDS) - words(query)
    return (e.identifier == "video-title" and "watch?v=" in e.value
            and not banned and length is not None and 60 <= length <= 1500)


def score(query, e):
    return 2 * len(words(query) & words(e.title)) + (1 if "official" in e.title.lower() else 0)


def choose_result(query, elems):
    return max(filter(partial(acceptable, query), elems), key=partial(score, query), default=None)


def is_pause(e):
    return e.title.startswith("Pause") and "button" in e.role.lower()


def is_ad_marker(e):
    return e.title in AD_TITLES or e.description in AD_TITLES


def is_search_box(e):
    return e.title == "Search" and "combobox" in e.role.lower()


def is_search_button(e):
    return e.title == "Search" and "button" in e.role.lower()


def controls_ready(c):
    return c[0] is not None and c[1] is not None


def frame_center(frame):
    nums = tuple(map(int, re.findall(r"-?\d+", frame)))
    return (nums[0] + nums[2] // 2, nums[1] + nums[3] // 2) if len(nums) == 4 else (637, 540)


def clock_seconds(groups):
    h, m, s = map(lambda g: int(g or 0), groups)
    return h * 3600 + m * 60 + s


def parse_slider(text):
    m = SLIDER_RE.search(text)
    return None if m is None else (clock_seconds(m.groups()[:3]), clock_seconds(m.groups()[3:]))


def believe(reading, first_seen, hint):
    return (reading is not None
            and reading.dur >= 60
            and (hint is None or abs(reading.dur - hint) <= 3)
            and first_seen - 10 <= reading.t - reading.pos <= first_seen + 60)


def deadline_for(start, dur):
    return start + dur - END_MARGIN - PAUSE_LATENCY


def pick_target(natural, cap):
    return natural if cap is None else min(natural, cap)


def resync(start, dur, r2):
    ok = (r2 is not None and abs(r2.dur - dur) <= 1
          and abs((r2.t - r2.pos) - start) <= 10)
    return r2.t - r2.pos if ok else start


def build_record(kind, idx, song, extra, now):
    return {"t": now, "stage": "exploitation", "source": "solution", "kind": kind,
            "song_index": idx, "song": song, **extra}


def parse_args(argv):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--songs", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--max-songs", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--forever", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--start-index", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--max-play-seconds", type=float, default=None)
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- effects

def b4(*parts):
    prefix = json.loads(os.environ["YUO_B4"])
    pid = os.environ["YUO_CHROME_PID"]
    args = (*parts, "--pid", pid)
    proc = subprocess.run([*prefix, *args], capture_output=True)
    return Result(proc.returncode,
                  proc.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
                  proc.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))


def b4_many(arglists):
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
        return tuple(pool.map(lambda a: b4(*a), arglists))


def emit(kind, idx, song, **extra):
    record = build_record(kind, idx, song, extra, time.time())
    with open(os.environ["YUO_EVENTS"], "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


def sleep_until(t):
    time.sleep(max(0.0, t - time.time()))


def read_text(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
        return fh.read()


def locate_player():
    res = b4("find", "--identifier", "movie_player", "--depth", "40",
             "--limit", "1", "--format", "xml")
    return first(elems_of(res, xml=True))


def observe():
    player = locate_player()
    if player is None:
        return Obs(False, False)
    ad_calls = tuple(map(
        lambda t: ("find", "--under", player.path, "--depth", "5", "--limit", "10", "--title", t),
        ("Sponsored", "My Ad Center", "Skip")))
    pause_call = ("find", "--role", "button", "--title", "Pause", "--depth", "40", "--limit", "5")
    results = b4_many((*ad_calls, pause_call))
    ads = itertools.chain.from_iterable(map(elems_of, results[:3]))
    return Obs(any(map(is_pause, elems_of(results[3]))), any(map(is_ad_marker, ads)))


def read_once():
    player = locate_player()
    if player is None:
        return None
    cx, cy = frame_center(player.frame)
    b4("activate")
    b4("hover", "--x", str(cx - 40), "--y", str(cy))
    b4("hover", "--x", str(cx), "--y", str(cy))
    time.sleep(0.8)
    res = b4("find", "--title", "Seek slider", "--role", "slider",
             "--under", player.path, "--depth", "8", "--limit", "1")
    t = time.time()
    slider = first(elems_of(res))
    parsed = None if slider is None else parse_slider(slider.value)
    return None if parsed is None else Reading(parsed[0], parsed[1], t)


def fetch_after(query, delay):
    time.sleep(delay)
    res = b4("find", "--role", "link", "--identifier", "video-title",
             "--depth", "40", "--limit", "25")
    return choose_result(query, elems_of(res))


def probe_controls(delay):
    time.sleep(delay)
    boxes, buttons = b4_many((
        ("find", "--role", "combobox", "--title", "Search", "--depth", "40", "--limit", "8"),
        ("find", "--role", "button", "--title", "Search", "--depth", "40", "--limit", "8"),
    ))
    return (first(filter(is_search_box, elems_of(boxes))),
            first(filter(is_search_button, elems_of(buttons))))


def open_result(job):
    b4("activate")
    box, button = next(
        filter(controls_ready,
               map(probe_controls, itertools.chain((0.0,), repeat(2.0, 12)))),
        (None, None))
    if box is None or button is None:
        return Opened(None, "search controls not found")
    typed = b4("set-value", "--path", box.path, "--value", job.query,
               "--expect-description", "Search")
    if typed.code != 0:
        return Opened(None, "set-value failed: " + typed.err.strip()[:120])
    submitted = b4("press", "--path", button.path, "--expect-description", "Search")
    if submitted.code != 0:
        return Opened(None, "search submit failed: " + submitted.err.strip()[:120])
    chosen = first(filter(lambda c: c is not None,
                          map(partial(fetch_after, job.query), (2.5, 1.5, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0))))
    if chosen is None:
        return Opened(None, "no suitable video result")
    pressed = b4("press", "--path", chosen.path,
                 "--expect-description", chosen.description or chosen.title)
    if pressed.code != 0:
        return Opened(None, "opening result failed: " + pressed.err.strip()[:120])
    return Opened(chosen, "")


def wait_step(job, prev, _):
    time.sleep(1.0)
    t0 = time.time()
    obs = observe()
    t = (t0 + time.time()) / 2
    if obs.ad and not prev.ad_seen:
        emit("ad_seen", job.idx, job.query)
    return WaitState(obs, t, prev.ad_seen or obs.ad, prev.n + 1)


def try_open(job, _n):
    opened = open_result(job)
    if opened.chosen is None:
        return Attempt(None, opened.reason)
    stream = accumulate(repeat(None, 90), partial(wait_step, job),
                        initial=WaitState(Obs(False, False), 0.0, False, 0))
    ready = next(dropwhile(lambda w: not (w.obs.playing and not w.obs.ad), stream), None)
    if ready is None:
        return Attempt(None, "playback not detected")
    return Attempt(Started(ready.t, duration_from_title(opened.chosen.title)), "")


def read_step(started, prev, _):
    time.sleep(0.0 if prev.tries == 0 else 3.0)
    r = read_once()
    return ReadState(r, believe(r, started.first_seen, started.hint), prev.tries + 1)


def resync_phase(start, dur, target):
    if target - 15.0 - time.time() < 2.0:
        return start
    sleep_until(target - 15.0)
    return resync(start, dur, read_once())


def try_pause(_):
    res = b4("find", "--role", "button", "--title", "Pause", "--depth", "40", "--limit", "5")
    btn = first(filter(is_pause, elems_of(res)))
    if btn is None:
        return None
    pressed = b4("press", "--path", btn.path, "--expect-description", btn.description or btn.title)
    return time.time() if pressed.code == 0 else None


def play_phase(job, started):
    stream = accumulate(repeat(None, 40), partial(read_step, started),
                        initial=ReadState(None, False, 0))
    good = next(filter(lambda s: s.believed, stream), None)
    reading = None if good is None else good.reading
    start, dur = ((reading.t - reading.pos, reading.dur) if reading is not None
                  else (started.first_seen, started.hint))
    if dur is None:
        emit("step_error", job.idx, job.query, reason="video duration unknown")
        return
    extra = {} if reading is None else {"position": round(reading.pos + time.time() - reading.t, 1)}
    emit("playback_started", job.idx, job.query, **extra)
    natural = deadline_for(start, dur)
    cap = None if job.max_play is None else started.first_seen + job.max_play
    target1 = pick_target(natural, cap)
    start2 = start if (cap is not None and cap < natural) else resync_phase(start, dur, target1)
    sleep_until(pick_target(deadline_for(start2, dur), cap))
    done = next(filter(lambda t: t is not None, map(try_pause, range(3))), None)
    if done is None:
        emit("step_error", job.idx, job.query, reason="pause failed")
        return
    emit("paused", job.idx, job.query, duration=dur, remaining=round(start2 + dur - done, 2))


def play_song(job):
    attempts = accumulate(takewhile(lambda n: n < 3, count()),
                          lambda prev, n: prev if prev.started is not None else try_open(job, n),
                          initial=Attempt(None, "not tried"))
    final = reduce(lambda _, x: x, attempts)
    if final.started is None:
        emit("step_error", job.idx, job.query,
             reason="could not find or play song: " + final.reason)
        return
    play_phase(job, final.started)


def run_song(job):
    emit("song_assigned", job.idx, job.query)
    try:
        play_song(job)
    except Exception as exc:
        emit("step_error", job.idx, job.query, reason="unexpected error: " + str(exc)[:200])


def main(argv):
    args = parse_args(argv)
    songs = parse_songs(read_text(args.songs))
    if not songs:
        return 1
    limit = None if args.forever else args.max_songs
    positions = islice(cycle(range(len(songs))), args.start_index % len(songs), None)
    jobs = map(lambda i: Job(i, songs[i], args.max_play_seconds), islice(positions, limit))
    tuple(map(run_song, jobs))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

Write solution.py: a standalone Python 3.13 program (standard library only) that plays a list of YouTube songs in an already-open Google Chrome using only blindly4 — no LLM, no network access of its own.

Command line: --songs FILE (UTF-8, one search query per line; skip blank lines and lines starting with #), --max-songs N (stop after N songs; without it, play forever), --forever (explicit forever), --start-index N (first list position, default 0), --max-play-seconds S (testing only: pause S seconds after playback starts if that comes first).

Behaviour, per song, looping over the list forever (itertools.cycle):
1. Emit song_assigned BEFORE any blindly4 call for that song.
2. Search YouTube for the query and open the right video: the song itself (official video/audio or a normal upload), not a mix, playlist, Short, live stream or loop. If pressing a result is refused (exit 64), try the next good result.
3. Ads: while an ad runs, press the player's Skip button as soon as it is there and enabled (a button inside movie_player whose identifier starts with skip-button; press it with --expect-description Skip); otherwise wait. Then make sure the song plays from its beginning (press the player's Play (k) button if that is what it shows); emit playback_started when you see the song itself playing (include "position" if known).
4. Wait until 3 seconds before the end of the video, then pause it; emit paused with "duration" (video length in seconds you used) and "remaining" (seconds left by your computation). Find the pause control early — at the re-sync 15 s before the deadline — inside the player (find --under <movie_player path> --title Pause --limit 1; with --limit above 1 blindly4 walks the whole tree, which can take seconds on a busy page) and keep that remembered path; at the deadline press the remembered path with --expect-description "Pause (k)" and search again only if that press fails.
5. Then the next song. Bound each search-and-start attempt by wall time (at most 120 s, measured with time.monotonic), make at most 3 attempts per song, and emit step_error with a "reason" after each failed attempt. After a step_error, back off before going on (5 s, doubling up to 60 s while failures repeat); if every song of a whole pass through the list failed, exit with a nonzero status.
Exit with status 0 after --max-songs songs.
Watchdog: the harness stops solution.py after 600 s without any event and without any blindly4 call (while a song confirmed playing plays out, its length plus 3 minutes).

The browser: Chrome is already open on YouTube; its process id is in the environment variable YUO_CHROME_PID. Never open or close the browser.
blindly4: call it ONLY through the command prefix in the environment variable YUO_B4 (a JSON array of strings): subprocess.run([*prefix, *args], capture_output=True) with args a blindly4 argument list that includes "--pid", pid. Decode stdout/stderr as UTF-8. stdout is JSON (XML with --format xml). Exit codes: 0 ok, 64 usage error or refused by the safety guard, 77 accessibility error (target gone, not foreground, ...).
Every call except apps and schema must include --pid with the YUO_CHROME_PID value; the proxy refuses calls aimed at any other window.
The proxy refuses: type, click, paste; press/set-value/focus without --expect-description; labels that start with, or are fragments of, subscribe, like, dislike, share, save, join, comment, reply, report, sign in, buy, premium, download, thanks, clip, remix, notify, create, upload; keys other than escape, f5, a digit, or return/enter given with --target-path and --require-value.
Keyboard and pointer input (key, hover, scroll) need Chrome in the foreground: run "activate" first when needed.
Tree paths change whenever the page changes: find an element again right before acting on it; when reusing a remembered path, check it first and fall back to find.
Read-only lookups may run concurrently (concurrent.futures; the first successful result wins); input commands must run one at a time.

Events: append one JSON object per line to the file named in the environment variable YUO_EVENTS (UTF-8; open, append, close each time):
{"t": time.time(), "stage": "exploitation", "source": "solution", "kind": KIND, "song_index": list position, "song": query, ...extra fields}
KIND is one of song_assigned, playback_started, paused, ad_seen, step_error.

Style — functional programming (checked by a linter; violations are rejected):
- Pure functions for parsing, matching and decisions; side effects (blindly4 calls, clock, sleep, event writes) confined to a small, clearly named set of effect functions.
- Immutable data only: @dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple, tuples, frozenset. No mutable globals.
- Use lambdas (at least 5), map/filter, functools.reduce, functools.partial, itertools (cycle, islice, repeat, takewhile, dropwhile, count), and a compose/pipe helper.
- Forbidden: while loops (iterate lazily: e.g. next(filter(ready, map(probe, itertools.repeat(None))))), global, nonlocal, augmented assignment (+= etc.), del, item or attribute assignment, mutating methods (append, extend, insert, pop, remove, clear, update, setdefault, popitem, add, discard, sort, reverse), classes other than frozen dataclasses / NamedTuple / Enum.
- Forbidden imports: anthropic, openai, requests, urllib, http, socket, httpx, aiohttp, ctypes, _ctypes, cffi, comtypes, pywinauto, uiautomation, win32*, pythoncom, pywintypes, _winapi, nt, posix, pyautogui, pynput, keyboard, mouse, selenium, playwright, webbrowser, asyncio, importlib, multiprocessing, ssl and other network modules; no __import__/eval/exec/compile/globals/locals/vars, no dunder names or attributes (__dict__, __builtins__, ...) other than __name__, no sys.modules; no os.system/os.popen/os.startfile/os.spawn*/os.exec*; no string mentioning claude, codex or blindly4.exe.
- Every subprocess call is a direct call (not via partial or an alias) whose command is exactly [*prefix, *args], where prefix = json.loads(os.environ["YUO_B4"]) is a name bound nowhere else (not a parameter, not a loop variable, not assigned anything else) and is used whole — never index or slice it. Use the subprocess and os modules only as subprocess.<name> / os.<name>, never as values.


How the exploration stage's own code decided that the song itself was playing and timed the pause (the timer's calls appear in the trace with origin "driver"):
- Ads: an ad is running while the player (the element with identifier movie_player; search inside it with find --under <its path> --depth 5) contains an element titled exactly "Sponsored", "My Ad Center", "Skip", "Skip Ad" or "Skip Ads". Unskippable ads show a Pause (k) button and no Skip button, so a Pause (k) button alone does not mean the song is playing: it is playing when Pause (k) is shown and no ad marker is. Short bumper ads (about 5 s) show no marker at all, and after an ad YouTube can take several more seconds to load the song.
- Right after playback was confirmed it hovered the pointer over the centre of the YouTube player ("hover" with the player element's frame centre) and then read the player's seek slider; the slider's value text ("X Minutes Y Seconds of A Minutes B Seconds") is only up to date right after such a hover — without it the text can be stale, even showing a finished ad.
- It computed start = now − position and deadline = start + duration − 3 s − 0.6 s (the pause call's own latency), slept until 15 s before the deadline, hovered and read again to re-sync, slept until the deadline, then pressed the pause control.
- Even right after a hover the text is sometimes stale, so a reading was believed for the start only if it was song-length (duration at least 60 s) and the start it implied (now − position) lay between 10 s before and 60 s after the moment the song was first seen playing with no ad marker. Until a reading was believed it kept taking readings every 5 s, up to 40. Hover by moving across the player (e.g. 40 px left of its centre, then the centre) and wait about 0.8 s before reading.
- The re-sync reading 15 s before the deadline moved the pause only if its duration was within 3 s of the duration in use and the start it implied agreed with the start in use within 10 s; otherwise the earlier estimate was kept.
- For solution.py, do better than a fixed anchor: measure that window from the last time an ad marker or an ad-length reading was seen (a reading whose duration is under 60 s or does not match the video's length proves the song has not started yet), and never fall back to the first ad-free moment while readings are still ad-length — keep reading instead, within the attempt's time budget.

Write solution.py: a standalone Python 3.13 program (standard library only) that plays a list of YouTube songs in an already-open Google Chrome using only blindly4 — no LLM, no network access of its own.

Command line: --songs FILE (UTF-8, one search query per line; skip blank lines and lines starting with #), --max-songs N (stop after N songs; without it, play forever), --forever (explicit forever), --start-index N (first list position, default 0), --max-play-seconds S (testing only: pause S seconds after playback starts if that comes first).

Behaviour, per song, looping over the list forever (itertools.cycle):
1. Emit song_assigned BEFORE any blindly4 call for that song.
2. Search YouTube for the query and open the right video: the song itself (official video/audio or a normal upload), not a mix, playlist, Short, live stream or loop. If pressing a result is refused (exit 64), try the next good result.
3. Ads: while an ad runs, press the player's Skip button as soon as it is there and enabled (a button inside movie_player whose identifier starts with skip-button; press it with --expect-description Skip); otherwise wait. Then make sure the song plays from its beginning (press the player's Play (k) button if that is what it shows); emit playback_started when you see the song itself playing (include "position" if known).
4. Wait until 3 seconds before the end of the video, then pause it; emit paused with "duration" (video length in seconds you used) and "remaining" (seconds left by your computation). Find the pause control early — at the re-sync 15 s before the deadline — inside the player (find --under <movie_player path> --title Pause --limit 1; with --limit above 1 blindly4 walks the whole tree, which can take seconds on a busy page) and keep that remembered path; at the deadline press the remembered path with --expect-description "Pause (k)" and search again only if that press fails.
5. Then the next song. Bound each search-and-start attempt by wall time (at most 120 s, measured with time.monotonic), make at most 3 attempts per song, and emit step_error with a "reason" after each failed attempt. After a step_error, back off before going on (5 s, doubling up to 60 s while failures repeat); if every song of a whole pass through the list failed, exit with a nonzero status.
Exit with status 0 after --max-songs songs.
Watchdog: the harness stops solution.py after 600 s without any event and without any blindly4 call (while a song confirmed playing plays out, its length plus 3 minutes).

The browser: Chrome is already open on YouTube; its process id is in the environment variable YUO_CHROME_PID. Never open or close the browser.
blindly4: call it ONLY through the command prefix in the environment variable YUO_B4 (a JSON array of strings): subprocess.run([*prefix, *args], capture_output=True) with args a blindly4 argument list that includes "--pid", pid. Decode stdout/stderr as UTF-8. stdout is JSON (XML with --format xml). Exit codes: 0 ok, 64 usage error or refused by the safety guard, 77 accessibility error (target gone, not foreground, ...).
Every call except apps and schema must include --pid with the YUO_CHROME_PID value; the proxy refuses calls aimed at any other window.
The proxy refuses: type, click, paste; press/set-value/focus without --expect-description; labels that start with, or are fragments of, subscribe, like, dislike, share, save, join, comment, reply, report, sign in, buy, premium, download, thanks, clip, remix, notify, create, upload; keys other than escape, f5, a digit, or return/enter given with --target-path and --require-value.
Keyboard and pointer input (key, hover, scroll) need Chrome in the foreground: run "activate" first when needed.
Tree paths change whenever the page changes: find an element again right before acting on it; when reusing a remembered path, check it first and fall back to find.
Read-only lookups may run concurrently (concurrent.futures; the first successful result wins); input commands must run one at a time.

Events: append one JSON object per line to the file named in the environment variable YUO_EVENTS (UTF-8; open, append, close each time):
{"t": time.time(), "stage": "exploitation", "source": "solution", "kind": KIND, "song_index": list position, "song": query, ...extra fields}
KIND is one of song_assigned, playback_started, paused, ad_seen, step_error.

- Immutable data only: @dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple, tuples, frozenset. No mutable globals.
