How the exploration stage's own code decided that the song itself was playing and timed the pause (the timer's calls appear in the trace with origin "driver"):
- Ads: an ad is running while the player (the element with identifier movie_player; search inside it with find --under <its path> --depth 5) contains an element titled exactly "Sponsored", "My Ad Center", "Skip", "Skip Ad" or "Skip Ads". Unskippable ads show a Pause (k) button and no Skip button, so a Pause (k) button alone does not mean the song is playing: it is playing when Pause (k) is shown and no ad marker is. Short bumper ads (about 5 s) show no marker at all, and after an ad YouTube can take several more seconds to load the song.
- Right after playback was confirmed it hovered the pointer over the centre of the YouTube player ("hover" with the player element's frame centre) and then read the player's seek slider; the slider's value text ("X Minutes Y Seconds of A Minutes B Seconds") is only up to date right after such a hover — without it the text can be stale, even showing a finished ad.
- It computed start = now − position and deadline = start + duration − 3 s − 0.6 s (the pause call's own latency), slept until 15 s before the deadline, hovered and read again to re-sync, slept until the deadline, then pressed the pause control.
- Even right after a hover the text is sometimes stale, so a reading was believed for the start only if it was song-length (duration at least 60 s) and the start it implied (now − position) lay between 10 s before and 60 s after the moment the song was first seen playing with no ad marker. Until a reading was believed it kept taking readings every 5 s, up to 40. Hover by moving across the player (e.g. 40 px left of its centre, then the centre) and wait about 0.8 s before reading.
- The re-sync reading 15 s before the deadline moved the pause only if its duration was within 3 s of the duration in use and the start it implied agreed with the start in use within 10 s; otherwise the earlier estimate was kept.
- For solution.py, do better than a fixed anchor: measure that window from the last time an ad marker or an ad-length reading was seen (a reading whose duration is under 60 s or does not match the video's length proves the song has not started yet), and never fall back to the first ad-free moment while readings are still ad-length — keep reading instead, within the attempt's time budget.

Write the complete solution.py. Reply with {"code": "<the whole file>"}.

Write solution.py: a standalone Python 3.13 program (standard library only) that plays a list of YouTube songs in an already-open Google Chrome using only blindly4 — no LLM, no network access of its own.

Command line: --songs FILE (UTF-8, one search query per line; skip blank lines and lines starting with #), --max-songs N (stop after N songs; without it, play forever), --forever (explicit forever), --start-index N (first list position, default 0), --max-play-seconds S (testing only: pause S seconds after playback starts if that comes first).

Behaviour, per song, looping over the list forever (itertools.cycle):
1. Emit song_assigned BEFORE any blindly4 call for that song.
2. Search YouTube for the query and open the right video: the song itself (official video/audio or a normal upload), not a mix, playlist, Short, live stream or loop. If pressing a result is refused (exit 64), try the next good result.
3. Ads: while an ad runs, press the player's Skip button as soon as it is there and enabled (a button inside movie_player whose identifier starts with skip-button; press it with --expect-description Skip); otherwise wait. Then make sure the song plays from its beginning (press the player's Play (k) button if that is what it shows); emit playback_started when you see the song itself playing (include "position" if known).
4. Wait until 3 seconds before the end of the video, then pause it; emit paused with "duration" (video length in seconds you used) and "remaining" (seconds left by your computation). Find the pause control early — at the re-sync 15 s before the deadline — inside the player (find --under <movie_player path> --title Pause --limit 1; with --limit above 1 blindly4 walks the whole tree, which can take seconds on a busy page) and keep that remembered path; at the deadline press the remembered path with --expect-description "Pause (k)" and search again only if that press fails.
5. Then the next song. Bound each search-and-start attempt by wall time (at most 120 s, measured with time.monotonic), make at most 3 attempts per song, and emit step_error with a "reason" after each failed attempt. After a step_error, back off before going on (5 s, doubling up to 60 s while failures repeat); if every song of a whole pass through the list failed, exit with a nonzero status.
Exit with status 0 after --max-songs songs.
Watchdog: the harness stops solution.py after 600 s without any event and without any blindly4 call (while a song confirmed playing plays out, its length plus 3 minutes).

The browser: Chrome is already open on YouTube; its process id is in the environment variable YUO_CHROME_PID. Never open or close the browser.
blindly4: call it ONLY through the command prefix in the environment variable YUO_B4 (a JSON array of strings): subprocess.run([*prefix, *args], capture_output=True) with args a blindly4 argument list that includes "--pid", pid. Decode stdout/stderr as UTF-8. stdout is JSON (XML with --format xml). Exit codes: 0 ok, 64 usage error or refused by the safety guard, 77 accessibility error (target gone, not foreground, ...).
Every call except apps and schema must include --pid with the YUO_CHROME_PID value; the proxy refuses calls aimed at any other window.
The proxy refuses: type, click, paste; press/set-value/focus without --expect-description; labels that start with, or are fragments of, subscribe, like, dislike, share, save, join, comment, reply, report, sign in, buy, premium, download, thanks, clip, remix, notify, create, upload; keys other than escape, f5, a digit, or return/enter given with --target-path and --require-value.
Keyboard and pointer input (key, hover, scroll) need Chrome in the foreground: run "activate" first when needed.
Tree paths change whenever the page changes: find an element again right before acting on it; when reusing a remembered path, check it first and fall back to find.
Read-only lookups may run concurrently (concurrent.futures; the first successful result wins); input commands must run one at a time.

Events: append one JSON object per line to the file named in the environment variable YUO_EVENTS (UTF-8; open, append, close each time):
{"t": time.time(), "stage": "exploitation", "source": "solution", "kind": KIND, "song_index": list position, "song": query, ...extra fields}
KIND is one of song_assigned, playback_started, paused, ad_seen, step_error.

Style — functional programming (checked by a linter; violations are rejected):
- Pure functions for parsing, matching and decisions; side effects (blindly4 calls, clock, sleep, event writes) confined to a small, clearly named set of effect functions.
- Immutable data only: @dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple, tuples, frozenset. No mutable globals.
- Use lambdas (at least 5), map/filter, functools.reduce, functools.partial, itertools (cycle, islice, repeat, takewhile, dropwhile, count), and a compose/pipe helper.
- Forbidden: while loops (iterate lazily: e.g. next(filter(ready, map(probe, itertools.repeat(None))))), global, nonlocal, augmented assignment (+= etc.), del, item or attribute assignment, mutating methods (append, extend, insert, pop, remove, clear, update, setdefault, popitem, add, discard, sort, reverse), classes other than frozen dataclasses / NamedTuple / Enum.
- Forbidden imports: anthropic, openai, requests, urllib, http, socket, httpx, aiohttp, ctypes, _ctypes, cffi, comtypes, pywinauto, uiautomation, win32*, pythoncom, pywintypes, _winapi, nt, posix, pyautogui, pynput, keyboard, mouse, selenium, playwright, webbrowser, asyncio, importlib, multiprocessing, ssl and other network modules; no __import__/eval/exec/compile/globals/locals/vars, no dunder names or attributes (__dict__, __builtins__, ...) other than __name__, no sys.modules; no os.system/os.popen/os.startfile/os.spawn*/os.exec*; no string mentioning claude, codex or blindly4.exe.
- Every subprocess call is a direct call (not via partial or an alias) whose command is exactly [*prefix, *args], where prefix = json.loads(os.environ["YUO_B4"]) is a name bound nowhere else (not a parameter, not a loop variable, not assigned anything else) and is used whole — never index or slice it. Use the subprocess and os modules only as subprocess.<name> / os.<name>, never as values.


How the exploration stage's own code decided that the song itself was playing and timed the pause (the timer's calls appear in the trace with origin "driver"):
- Ads: an ad is running while the player (the element with identifier movie_player; search inside it with find --under <its path> --depth 5) contains an element titled exactly "Sponsored", "My Ad Center", "Skip", "Skip Ad" or "Skip Ads". Unskippable ads show a Pause (k) button and no Skip button, so a Pause (k) button alone does not mean the song is playing: it is playing when Pause (k) is shown and no ad marker is. Short bumper ads (about 5 s) show no marker at all, and after an ad YouTube can take several more seconds to load the song.
- Right after playback was confirmed it hovered the pointer over the centre of the YouTube player ("hover" with the player element's frame centre) and then read the player's seek slider; the slider's value text ("X Minutes Y Seconds of A Minutes B Seconds") is only up to date right after such a hover — without it the text can be stale, even showing a finished ad.
- It computed start = now − position and deadline = start + duration − 3 s − 0.6 s (the pause call's own latency), slept until 15 s before the deadline, hovered and read again to re-sync, slept until the deadline, then pressed the pause control.
- Even right after a hover the text is sometimes stale, so a reading was believed for the start only if it was song-length (duration at least 60 s) and the start it implied (now − position) lay between 10 s before and 60 s after the moment the song was first seen playing with no ad marker. Until a reading was believed it kept taking readings every 5 s, up to 40. Hover by moving across the player (e.g. 40 px left of its centre, then the centre) and wait about 0.8 s before reading.
- The re-sync reading 15 s before the deadline moved the pause only if its duration was within 3 s of the duration in use and the start it implied agreed with the start in use within 10 s; otherwise the earlier estimate was kept.
- For solution.py, do better than a fixed anchor: measure that window from the last time an ad marker or an ad-length reading was seen (a reading whose duration is under 60 s or does not match the video's length proves the song has not started yet), and never fall back to the first ad-free moment while readings are still ad-length — keep reading instead, within the attempt's time budget.

blindly4 commands available through YUO_B4:
blindly4 schema — Print command metadata. Windows UIA retains AX role/action names for compatibility. [read-only]
blindly4 request-permission — Windows UI Automation needs no macOS permission. Elevated and secure desktops remain inaccessible. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 apps — List visible GUI applications and PIDs. [read-only]
blindly4 activate --pid PID — Bring an application to the foreground and verify it. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 open --url URL [--chrome-profile DIR] — Open an HTTP, HTTPS or Slack URL; --chrome-profile launches an isolated, accessible Chrome and reports its pid. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 tree [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--format json|xml] — Read a bounded live accessibility tree; --format xml prints the XML UI tree. [read-only]
blindly4 show [--pid PID] [--depth N] — Print a readable live outline with paths. [read-only]
blindly4 find [--title TEXT] [--role ROLE] [--value TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--identifier ID] [--under PATH] [--pid PID] [--depth N] [--limit N] [--format json|xml] — Search current accessible properties; --identifier is exact, --under limits the search to one subtree. [read-only]
blindly4 focused [--pid PID] — Read the focused control without changing focus. [read-only]
blindly4 inspect --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Inspect one live element. [read-only]
blindly4 actions --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — List supported actions. [read-only]
blindly4 focus --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] — Focus an element. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 show-menu --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Expand an accessible menu control when supported. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll-to --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] — Scroll an accessible item into view. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 press --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] [--expect-description TEXT] [--require-selected] [--require-value-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Invoke or select a control; may submit external data. [external-commit]
blindly4 set-value --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT [--expect-description TEXT] — Set a writable ValuePattern. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 set-selected-text --path INDEX[.INDEX...] [--pid PID] --value TEXT — Replace selected text in a focused writable control. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 click --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Click a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 hover --x X --y Y [--pid PID] — Move the pointer, without clicking, to a screen coordinate in the verified target application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 type --text TEXT [--pid PID] — Inject Unicode text into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 paste --text TEXT [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH] — Paste, optionally verifying an exact writable target draft. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 scroll --direction up|down|left|right [--amount LINES] [--pid PID] — Inject bounded wheel input into the foreground application. [ui-mutation]
blindly4 key --key KEY [--pid PID] [--target-path PATH --require-value TEXT] — Inject a key; a guarded key requires exact focused draft and PID. [external-commit]
